source.title: Obtaining transferable chemical insight from solving machine-learning classification problems: Thermodynamical properties prediction, atomic composition as good as Coulomb matrix
source.authors: León Alday-Toledo; R. Bernal-Jaquez; Saúl Zapotecas-Martínez; Jose L. Mendoza-Cortes

record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out classification performance under Adam and AdaBelief, a different optimizer comparison and task from the versions’ cited studies.
record.gate_note: Reports held-out classification rates and training-loss curves for molecular-property prediction. The curves do not give a directly comparable train-versus-test generalization gap. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study cites adaptive methods' poorer generalization than SGD as motivation, but compares only Adam with AdaBelief, both adaptive optimizers, on molecular-property classification. It supplies no SGD comparison or test of any other claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors conclude that AdaBelief is preferable for low-resolution descriptors, while high-resolution results depend much less on optimizer choice. This is a tendency, with a tie and a small Adam advantage in the tables. Their broader conclusion is that inexpensive molecular descriptors and suitable optimizers can suffice for coarse property classification, while heat-capacity prediction remains difficult.
record.recipe_differences: Three-hidden-layer sigmoid networks trained on QM9 molecular descriptors with default Adam or AdaBelief settings; molecular-property classification rather than the cited optimizer studies’ benchmark comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer effect varies by property and representation resolution; results are averaged across five cross-validation experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: With default optimizer settings, AdaBelief exceeds Adam on all low-resolution descriptor/property pairs: for example, enthalpy AC accuracy is 0.9921 versus 0.7279. High-resolution results are close, including an exact Gibbs-energy SCMAC tie and slightly better Adam performance on ZPVE SCM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On these QM9 molecular-property classification tasks, AdaBelief generally improves held-out accuracy over Adam, especially with low-resolution descriptors; differences are smaller for high-resolution descriptors.

record.problems: Only two optimizers are compared, using default hyperparameters; no SGD comparator. Results use classification rates for four specific molecular properties, not train-test error gaps. Cross-validation results are averaged over five experiments and no uncertainty estimates are reported.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and matched natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Width-dependent test error beyond the zero-training-error threshold; architecture selection here supplies no such sweep.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
All parts: no adaptive-versus-SGD comparison, tuning comparison, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, or word-level language-model experiment.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Effects of adding or removing dropout, including interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures.
Removal of memorized training examples versus equal-sized random removals and subsequent test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: All 40 extracted values and paired baselines match Tables 4–7. The invalid V4 links, rather than numerical extraction errors, require correction. Training-loss curves do not supply the missing SGD comparison. Reported results average five cross-validation experiments without uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label memorization comparison or natural-label train-versus-test accuracy comparison.
No width sweep around the zero-training-error threshold.
Compares Adam with AdaBelief only; no SGD or momentum SGD, language benchmarks, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or optimizer switching.
No sharpness, perturbation tolerance, or generalization-gap measure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Low-resolution representations for enthalpy, Gibbs’ free energy, and zero-point vibrational energy
reader_labels.reason: AdaBelief test classification rates exceed Adam for the paired low-resolution models, often substantially (R1–R6, R11–R16, R21–R26). This is an optimizer comparison, not the version’s Adam-versus-SGD comparison.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Low-resolution representations for constant-volume heat capacity, and high-resolution representations across all four properties
reader_labels.reason: AdaBelief's low-resolution improvement for heat capacity remains modest, while paired high-resolution scores are close or identical across the properties (R7–R10, R17–R20, R27–R30, R31–R40).
